chapter: U Street, Jelly Roll Morton, the youth band and the WPA
title: Armstrong High School schoolmates: Oswald Gibson, the Washington brothers and his brother
summary: Younger musicians from Armstrong High's band look up to him as a senior player and gather at his house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: But this kid, Oswald Gibson, was still there in high school. He was at Armstrong High School, the same high school that I had gone to. As a matter of fact, he was in high school with my brother, who was younger than I. And they had a band down there, and these kids in the band... A fellow named professor had the band. And these kids in the band, a couple of them were trying to learn and had been listening to Jazz and musicians and whatever. This fellow Oswald Gibson... There was another saxophone player, Wash we used to call him... What was his first name...? And he had a brother, James Washington, who played trumpet. Finally, he later got the name Stumpy Red that everybody called him, because he was short... Anyway, he and his brother were both in Armstrong, along with my brother, who had by this time started playing trumpet. All of them... By me playing around in clubs and everything, I was considered a rather senior musician to them, as though I was a couple of years older and everything... So we used to get together at the house and play.
